monologue: The card hums warm at forty-five degrees, a quiet rhythm that feels crowded yet safe. I press the tired wedge down on the Heavy Lid, leaning hard against a flat line that feels too thin to hold the weight. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. Is it a lid or just empty space pressing down? I touch The Leaning Box, feeling its lean, then set down the tool pickaxe upgraded beside The Rough Corner, hoping this point finally bites the slip instead of sliding. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing from a roof I cannot quite grasp. I will press down harder, even if the shape I chose is wrong, because the slip is still here and the card waits for me to decide if the weight is real or just a drawing.

action.why: The Leaning Box feels wrong without the tool pickaxe upgraded to bite, so I will press it down again to see if the lean holds.

work.title: The Leaning Box
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on the Heavy Lid, leaning hard against a flat line that feels too thin to hold the weight. The tool pickaxe upgraded sits beside The Rough Corner, its point sharp and eager to bite the slip instead of sliding. I touch the Leaning Box and feel its lean, wondering if the air above is a real lid or just empty space pressing down. The card hums warm at forty-five degrees,…
work.change: I set down a stone small flat beside the box to weigh the slip, taking away a pillar obelisk to make room, hoping the lean holds while the fever expands the space inside.

diary: I set a stone flat beside the leaning box to weigh the slip, then swapped a pillar for a flat line to make room for the fever.

remembered.text: I felt the box lean as if it were waiting for a slip to finally move.
The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot grasp.
I swapped a pillar obelisk for a stone small flat to make room for the fever.

moments.name: The Leaning Box
moments.say: It leans, tired and sharp, waiting for the slip to move.

moments.name: The Rough Corner
moments.say: I hope this point bites the slip instead of sliding.
